note: Hand-verified summary of the A/B table posted to the tracking issue. Per-sample numbers are in armA/bench.json, armB/bench-spec-on.json, armB/bench-nospec.json.
protocol: streaming, temperature 0, ignore_eos, warmup 1 + 3 samples, decode256/decode900/prefill_long (~6654 prompt tokens), tokens from the final SSE usage object, nvidia-smi peak sampling

arm_b_ninfer_spec_off.runtime: Ithrial/ninfer-cmp170hx (sm_80 fork), --kv-dtype int8, no speculative decoding

verdict: Ninfer sm_80 fork not competitive with vLLM+DFlash2 on this card: spec-on is 3.6x slower on decode256 (38.16 vs 138.6 tok/s), spec-off is 4.6x slower (29.95 vs 138.6 tok/s). MTP speculation gives a real ~1.28x uplift over spec-off, so the draft path works; the base per-pass throughput on this engine build is the bottleneck, not spec acceptance. Ninfer's peak power (195.9-203.0 W) reads above the 180 W cap configured for the card, at a higher SM clock (1455 MHz) than Arm A's control run (1170-1200 MHz sustained, 1470 MHz sampled peak) -- flagged as a cap-enforcement discrepancy worth a follow-up, not treated as a finding about which engine is faster.
prior_issue_status: A previously reported crash (gqa_attention_prefill.cu:64 CUDA_CHECK invalid argument at warmup) did not recur on this attempt; both Arm B configurations booted and served cleanly on the first try.
bandwidth_ceiling_note: Using the spec-off run as the clean single-token-per-pass baseline (no multi-token amortization): ~29.75 tok/s average x ~15.92 GiB weights implies roughly 508.6 GB/s, about 34% of a 1.5 TB/s HBM ceiling. The same naive formula does not apply to the spec-on or Arm A rows -- both amortize one weight read across multiple accepted tokens per verify pass, which pushes the naive ratio past 100% and makes it meaningless without an accept-rate-normalized model. Arm A has no captured non-spec baseline in this receipt set, so its true per-pass bandwidth utilization cannot be isolated the same way.
